question: Under stated marginal-burn assumptions, what destination price premium offsets tankering costs, and how much destination uplift can be displaced during a local supply interruption?

counterfactual.comparison: Buy q at destination versus carry enough extra origin fuel to deliver the same q at destination.
notEstablished: actual airport prices or available stocks
counterfactual.quantityBasis: One tonne useful fuel delivered at destination; local-interruption headroom is separately one tonne loaded at origin.

airportSnapshot.scope: Coordinates only; no airport fuel prices, fuel capacity, stock or flight schedules.

earthRadiusKm.note: Fixed spherical mean-Earth radius used for reproducible great-circle geometry; not an aircraft flight path.

burnCoefficientPerHour.source: ICAO Environmental Report 2022, Economic Fuel Tankering: A Threat to Aviation Decarbonisation, p.150, quoting ICAO Doc 10013 section 4.1.2.
burnCoefficientPerHour.limitation: Aircraft-dependent range of extra burn per additional weight per flight-hour, used as sensitivity bounds; no route or aircraft calibration.

co2TonnesPerTonneFuel.source: ICAO CORSIA FAQ section 3.59, Jet-A and Jet-A1 conversion factor.
co2TonnesPerTonneFuel.scope: Direct combustion CO2 only; excludes fuel lifecycle and non-CO2 climate effects.

speedKph.note: Groundspeed proxy, not observed flight performance.

pathFactor.note: Ratio of modelled airborne path to great-circle distance; no taxi, winds, climb or actual routing model.

controlledDurationH.note: Controlled time comparisons independent of the route-time proxy.

originPriceScenarioUsdPerT.note: Illustrative normalization for carbon-cost sensitivity, not an observed airport price. Zero-carbon, zero-fee ratio results do not depend on this reference level.

carbonUsdPerTCo2.note: Additional carbon charge or shadow value; not an observed carbon market price. Do not double count carbon already included in fuel prices.

extraCostUsdPerDeliveredT.note: Additional handling/payload opportunity cost per delivered tonne. Zero is a transparent lower-cost case, not evidence such costs vanish.

requiredDeliveryT.note: Normalization per useful tonne; no observation of an aircraft fuel requirement.

extraOriginHeadroomT.note: Separate local-interruption normalization; actual aircraft and supplier headroom remains unobserved.

models.note: Linear retention 1-k*t holds the initial marginal uplift weight as a burn reference; exponential retention exp(-k*t) allows marginal mass to decay. Neither is an aircraft-calibrated law. Linear is more fuel-intensive only relative to this exponential comparator.

outputInterpretation.localDisruption: Destination uplift displaced if origin has the extra supply/headroom. This does not infer flight continuation.
outputInterpretation.sharedQuota: For the same q delivered, tankering consumes q/a rather than q units from a shared regional fuel quota; the difference is burned. This resource identity is not a cancellation model and does not rule out benefits from reallocating scarce fuel geographically.
outputInterpretation.uncertainty: Finite sensitivity envelopes, not probabilistic confidence intervals or forecasts.
